purpose: Migrate two transient-based cache metrics (cache size, DB cleanup counts) to event-driven invalidation using WordPress 6.9's wp_cache_get_salted()/wp_cache_set_salted() with transient fallback for older WP versions.
riskRationale: The core feature code is clean and backward-compatible, but unrelated vendor changes delete platform_check.php and disable Composer's PHP 8.2 requirement check, which could cause fatal errors on incompatible hosts. The salt increment ordering issue in class-cache.php could produce stale metrics on failed cache clears.
breakingChanges: vendor/composer/platform_check.php deleted — bypasses PHP 8.2 requirement check

text: The core feature implementation is well-structured with consistent salted cache patterns, proper backward compatibility, and correct hook filtering across all three files. However, three issues block merge: (1) unrelated vendor changes that disable PHP version checking, (2) cache salt incremented before file deletion succeeds, and (3) save_post hook fires unconditionally on every post save. Two minor code cleanliness issues should also be addressed.

reasoning: Vendor file changes (platform_check.php deletion + autoloader modification) are entirely unrelated to the PR's purpose and bypass PHP 8.2 requirement checks. The salt ordering issue could produce stale cache metrics on failed clears. These must be fixed before merge. The feature implementation itself is solid.

message: Consistent dual-path pattern (salted cache on WP 6.9+, transient fallback on older WP) used across all three files, making the upgrade path clear and safe.
Hooks are registered unconditionally (outside the 'enableCache' guard), which is correct — DB cleanup count invalidation should fire on post changes regardless of page cache settings.
invoke_cleanup_method defers to invalidate_counts_cache() instead of inlining the logic, keeping the invalidation strategy centralized and reusable.
on_post_change() properly filters out revisions/autosaves and checks is_post_type_viewable(), avoiding unnecessary salt writes for non-content post types.

The require __DIR__ . '/platform_check.php' line has been removed and platform_check.php itself has been deleted. This disables Composer's PHP version requirement check (8.2+), allowing the plugin to load on PHP < 8.2 — which would cause fatal errors from code using PHP 8.2+ features. These changes are entirely unrelated to the PR's stated purpose.
suggestion: Revert all three vendor file changes: git checkout HEAD -- vendor/composer/autoload_real.php vendor/composer/installed.php vendor/composer/platform_check.php. If platform_check removal is intentional, it must be done in a separate, documented commit with clear rationale.
suggestionCode: git checkout HEAD -- vendor/composer/autoload_real.php vendor/composer/installed.php vendor/composer/platform_check.php

message: The cache salt is incremented before the actual cache file deletion. If the filesystem is unavailable or deletion fails, the salt is already incremented, causing a cache miss. On the next admin page load, get_cache_size() will recompute from disk — which still contains the old uncleared files — and cache that stale value as fresh, misleadingly showing the pre-clear size as newly computed.
suggestion: Move the salt increment and transient deletion to after the cache files are successfully deleted, so invalidation only happens if the clear actually succeeded.

message: The save_post and deleted_post hooks fire unconditionally on every post save/delete, including nav_menu_items, wp_block (reusable blocks), wp_template, and other internal post types. While is_post_type_viewable() in on_post_change() filters these out, the static method call on every admin post save adds unnecessary overhead.
suggestion: Wrap both hook registrations in an is_admin() check since DB cleanup counts are only consumed in the admin dashboard, or remove the guard entirely and keep the existing is_post_type_viewable() check as sufficient protection.

message: The non-atomic get_option()+1+update_option() salt increment pattern has a theoretical race condition where two concurrent calls could read the same value and both write the same incremented value. Additionally, the salt key string is duplicated as a literal in get_counts() and invalidate_counts_cache() instead of using a class constant.
suggestion: Use time() instead of increment for stronger cross-request uniqueness, and define a private const SALT_KEY to avoid string literal duplication.
suggestionCode: define( 'wppo_db_cleanup_salt' ) once; use time() for the value.

message: Function_exists guards are inconsistent: get_counts() checks wp_cache_get_salted, invalidate_counts_cache() checks wp_cache_get_salted, and the write path on line 717 checks wp_cache_set_salted. These functions ship together in WP 6.9, so checking different functions is unnecessary and could cause partial migration if one function is polyfilled independently.
suggestion: Consolidate all three checks to use wp_cache_get_salted, and assign the result to a local variable once to avoid repeated function_exists calls.

message: The $post parameter defaults to null but both save_post and deleted_post always provide the post object as the second argument. The fallback get_post_type($post_id) adds an unnecessary DB query on the unlikely edge case where a third-party plugin fires these hooks without the post parameter.
suggestion: Remove the $post = null default and type-hint as ?WP_Post $post = null for clarity.
